title: Marcos welcomes ‘old friend’ as Mandarin reopens
summary: Globally renowned hotel chain Mandarin Oriental reopened its doors yesterday, a development President Marcos described as a return of an “old friend” and an “expression of…

blocks.text: The Mandarin Oriental Makati opened its doors yesterday, 12 years after closing down. The iconic hotel is located at Ayala Triangle Gardens, just meters away from where it originally stood at the corner of Makati Avenue and Paseo de Roxas.

MANILA, Philippines — Globally renowned hotel chain Mandarin Oriental reopened its doors yesterday, a development President Marcos described as a return of an “old friend” and an “expression of confidence” in the Philippines.

Mandarin Oriental Makati, which started welcoming guests in 1976 but ceased operations in 2014, staged a comeback with a ceremony attended by Marcos, First Lady Liza Marcos and prominent personalities from the government and business sector.
The hotel added 275 guest rooms and suites to the Philippines’ accommodation inventory and is seen to generate 410 jobs.
“It is always a pleasure to welcome an old friend back home,” Marcos said in remarks delivered during the opening ceremony.

“The opening of this hotel is also a welcome expression of confidence in our country and in the future of Philippine tourism. When an established brand chooses to invest and grow here, it helps create opportunities that extend well
beyond the vicinity of its properties,” he added.

Marcos described Mandarin Oriental Manila as a landmark hotel and a venue for those who celebrated milestones, made memories, or simply came to have a rest. The contemporary hotel, located at the very heart of Ayala Triangle, combines Mandarin Oriental’s renowned tradition of service with the distinct character of Filipino craftsmanship, arts, and hospitality, he added.

Marcos thanked Ayala Land, Mandarin Oriental and all their partners who made the reopening possible and expressed hope that the hotel would be a gateway to Philippine culture, a source of opportunity and “another reason for the world to discover the best of the Filipino experience.
Also present during the event were Makati City Mayor Nancy Binay, Ayala Corp. chairman Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala and Mandarin Oriental officials.

The President cited the uniforms of the hotel staff designed by Rajo Laurel, shoes made by Marikina shoemakers, binakol robes crafted by artisans in Abra and guest rooms that showcase Filipino artistry and ingenuity.
“Through these distinctly Filipino elements, the hotel aims to offer both local and foreign guests a unique experience of what the Philippines has to offer,” Marcos said.

Marcos gave assurance that the administration is committed to strengthening the Philippine tourism and hospitality sector as a key driver of economic growth. He noted that the opening of hotels creates jobs and provides opportunities to micro, small and medium enterprises.

“Filipino service is recognized for its excellence around the world. Our goal is to have more visitors experience it firsthand right here in the Philippines. And to make this possible, we continue to improve connectivity and infrastructure, strengthen our investment environment and work with industry partners to raise the quality of our tourism offerings,” the Chief Executive said.

Marcos said the Philippines’ recent hosting of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit has proven that the Philippines is “well capable of welcoming the world and proudly doing so with smiles and with exceptional hospitality.”
“Let’s therefore build on that momentum, make the Philippines a more attractive destination in the region and beyond,” he said.
